clue.text: MGM's typical macho man? 16, hands down!

parts.note: a stud is a virile, macho man

indicators.note: both hands, left and right, are put down, so the outer letters of the word go

parts.note: 16-across is LION, the second half of 25-across

explanation.surface: A question about the swaggering he-man typical of an MGM film, with a call to put hands down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands down' removes the two ends of LION (16-across), leaving IO; MGM's famous roaring lion logo makes the cross-reference neat.
explanation.definitionFit: MGM is a classic example of a Hollywood film production company, so a typical one of its kind.

clue.text: Capital for transaction secured by partner, one in 5D's company

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, capital letter

parts.note: something secured by another is in it
a man is a partner, as in husband

explanation.surface: A finance phrase: capital for a deal is guaranteed by a business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal woodman seeking a heart walks with Dorothy, part of her company.

clue.text: Bishop and I so busy outside church

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go round the other piece
busy suggests letters bustling about into a new order

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A bishop and the speaker are kept very busy outside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, the word means a bishop in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: In error over rise, get someone independent to do it

definitions.text: get someone independent to do it

indicators.note: in a down entry over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to be out is to be wrong, as in a calculation
a river's rise is its source

explanation.surface: After a mistake over a pay rise, the boss hands the work to a contractor.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms contract out work to external suppliers rather than doing it in-house.

clue.text: Drips of understudies taking on board wizard's tips — re overacting for starters

indicators.note: taking on board means holding other letters within, like cargo in a ship

parts.note: understudies are deputies, abbreviated DEPS

indicators.note: the tips of the word wizard are its first and last letters
for starters takes the opening letter of each of the words re and overacting

explanation.surface: Theatre backstage: the understudies in a wizard show are told some tips about overacting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewdrops are small drops of moisture, so they are drips in the sense of falling beads of liquid.

clue.text: 25 bloke excitedly touring Rhode Island; for him, and four others here, a fantastic route, but uphill all the way!

indicators.note: touring means the scrambled letters go all round the other piece
excitedly suggests letters jumping about into a new order

parts.note: 25-across on its own is COWARDLY, followed by the word bloke as written
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A rambling travel note: a lion-hearted bloke tours Rhode Island on a fabulous uphill trail with four companions.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' is only the 25-across light, COWARDLY. 'uphill all the way' says the road is entered from bottom to top, so reads backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden road to the Emerald City in The Wizard of Oz is a famous fantasy path.

clue.text: Hot springs with fish circling one of 5D's troupe

indicators.note: circling means the fish goes round the other letters

parts.note: a dory is a sea fish, the John Dory

indicators.note: springs suggests letters leaping into a new order

explanation.surface: Hot springs where fish circle one of the travelling troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kansas girl is the central traveller, a member of the group on the road.

clue.text: With 'ideousness on the radio, I root around to find some music

indicators.note: on the radio means we hear the word spoken rather than see it

parts.note: hideousness is horror; with the H dropped it becomes 'orror

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Cockney-voiced complaint about awful radio sounds, while someone roots around for music.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in the clue tells us to drop it from the sounded word too.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale choral work, so it counts as some music.

clue.text: One in 5D's party has singular trouble over Conservative line

indicators.note: in a down entry over means the first pieces sit above the next

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
care means trouble or worry
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A political party member has trouble over a Conservative policy line.
explanation.definitionFit: The straw man who wants a brain joins Dorothy, one of the party travelling together.

clue.text: A couple of overs tore down madly, but put no opener in difficulty

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for overs

indicators.note: madly signals that the letters are thrown into a crazed new order
put no tells us to leave out a letter from the word down
the opener of difficulty is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a bowler charged in madly for a couple of overs but the opening batsman was never troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put no opener in difficulty' takes D from DOWN, leaving OWN; 'madly' scrambles O, TORE and OWN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a small number, roughly a couple or a few.

clue.text: Mysteries a rainbow's genesis is able to answer?

indicators.note: the genesis of a word is its beginning, here its first letter

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: is a rainbow's origin the kind of mystery that can be answered?
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are secrets or hidden knowledge, the sort of things known only to the initiated.

clue.text: Ruby's last drink with forward fellow offering security

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Ruby

parts.note: ale is a drink of beer
a lock is a forward in the second row of a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A pub scene: Ruby finishes her drink with a pushy man who offers her protection.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the lock is a forward in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name has become a generic term for a cylinder door fastening, a device giving security.

clue.text: In bewitched style, digressing from stately address

indicators.note: bewitched suggests letters put under a spell, so the word style can be lifted out in any order
the letters of style wander off out of the word stately, leaving only what remains

parts.note: a home is one's address

explanation.surface: A description of a stately home's manner, enchanted yet wandering from formal style.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of STYLE ('bewitched' means in any order) from STATELY, leaving AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in, as opposed to out, means being present at your own residence.

clue.text: Soak and squeeze calico cloth, dislodging rinds from Camembert

indicators.note: squeeze suggests letters crushed together into a new order
dislodging means some letters are knocked out of the cloth
the rinds of a cheese are its outside, so the first and last letters of Camembert

explanation.surface: Cheese-making instructions: soak and press a calico cloth, removing the rinds from a Camembert.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C and T (Camembert's rinds) out of CALICO CLOTH and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A soak is slang for a heavy drinker, a synonym for a drunkard.

clue.text: Notice Louis, maybe, at play with odd slippers — far from clumsily

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
Louis is an example of a French king, roi in French

indicators.note: the odd letters slip away, leaving the even ones of at play

explanation.surface: A French king, Louis perhaps, seen at play wearing mismatched slippers.
explanation.walkthrough: Eighteen French kings were called Louis, so a Louis may be a ROI.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with skill and dexterity is the opposite of doing it clumsily.

clue.text: Rented land using 16's capital to alleviate reserve

parts.note: 16-across is LION, whose capital or first letter is L
to ease is to alleviate
to hold is to reserve, as a seat

explanation.surface: Using a lion's money to ease a nature reserve's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Property held on a lease, for a fixed term against rent, is land that is rented.

clue.text: See 25
Run riot, as Alice does with cake?

definitions.meaning: plants that run riot spread out of control
in Alice in Wonderland a cake marked Eat Me makes Alice shoot up in size

explanation.surface: A question about Alice in Wonderland behaving wildly after eating cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden that runs riot becomes rampant, and Alice gets too big after the cake.

clue.text: Direct O'Toole in part as a member of the 5D band

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to cast Peter O'Toole in a film role as one of a travelling band.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy's little dog travels with her along the road, so he is one of the group of companions.

clue.text: Dry and rent-free?

definitions.meaning: rent read as a tear or rip, so without any rips

explanation.surface: A tenant describes a dry flat with no rent to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without crying means dry-eyed, and being without a rip means rent-free.

clue.text: Marvel's left note for Charlie during wrap for film

indicators.note: what is left at the beginning is the opening letter of Marvel
note for Charlie means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: to embrace is to wrap in one's arms
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A movie-industry snippet: Marvel leaves a memo during the wrap of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marvel' looks like the comics studio, and 'wrap' like the end of filming, but both are just letters and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A membrane is a thin layer or skin, like the thin film covering a surface.

clue.text: He uses arm vigorously!

indicators.note: vigorously suggests letters being kneaded hard into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a man pumping his arm hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a male massage therapist works hard with his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A male massage practitioner kneads muscles, energetically working his arms.

clue.text: Without unusual delay, cast leading lady star from Oz

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
without unusual says the letters of delay, in any order, are taken out

explanation.surface: Casting a leading lady without odd delays, a star from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' looks like Australia but is the land of the musical. Remove D, E, L, A, Y from LEADING LADY and rearrange LADING.
explanation.definitionFit: The Good Witch is a leading character in the story of the land ruled by the Wizard.

clue.text: Disturb badger bait

definitions.meaning: to disturb is to bother persistently
to badger is to pester repeatedly
to bait is to torment or tease

explanation.surface: Reads like an order to rouse a badger used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: All three verbs describe pestering someone, a synonym for each definition in turn.

clue.text: Disallow deliveries — pity — when crossing line

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: crossing here means one thing is set athwart the middle of another

parts.note: to rue is to regret or pity

explanation.surface: A sad cricket incident: deliveries disallowed because the bowler overstepped the line.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule a decision is to set it aside, so to disallow it.

clue.text: Buttery clafoutis waiter brought Adam for seconds, with depleted filling of cherry

indicators.note: for seconds picks the second letter of each of the four words
the filling of a word is its middle, depleted to just its central pair

explanation.surface: A restaurant scene: the waiter brings Adam a second helping of cherry clafoutis, short on filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttery' looks like an adjective about the pudding, but it is the noun for a food store.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttery is an old word for a storeroom for provisions, the same thing as a pantry.

clue.text: Munch noodles around Emerald's van, where one's idling

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the other letter
to munch is to chew, crushing the letters into a new order
the van is the front, so the first letter of Emerald

explanation.surface: Someone eating noodles around an Emerald City van while killing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loose end means having nothing to do, the state of someone idling.

clue.text: Transfer rugby player like Noel, one for 5D's team?

indicators.note: transfer says the pieces swap places, so the second one stated comes first

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright; cowardly read as Coward-ly means like him
a Lion is a player for the British and Irish Lions rugby team

explanation.surface: A sports transfer story: a rugby player compared to Noel Coward joins another team.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby union side picked from four nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The fearful big cat is one of the companions on the road to the Emerald City.

clue.text: It's awful to criticise Mum's Latin

parts.note: to dis is slang for to criticise
Ma is another word for mum

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is terrible to mock one's mother's Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy or dreadful, the quality of something awful.
